threeSecond.purpose: Athena is a guided tool that helps you turn a rough idea into a research question backed by real papers from PubMed and OpenAlex, through a 9-step process.

confusing: The three step cards show tiny diagrams with text too small to read, so I could not tell what they show.
The cards are labelled step 2, 6 and 7 of 9 but sit under 'Stage 1, 2, 3', so the steps versus stages numbering is confusing at a glance.
Words like 'appraise', 'synonyms', 'OpenAlex' and 'quotes checked against source' are jargon.
The faint scattered dots behind the headline looked like decoration or noise, and I could not tell what they mean.
It is not clear what 'I have an instruction' vs 'Start a review' means beyond new vs returning user (I read it as returning user).
The cards are cut off at the bottom of the screen.

Green seems to mean 'found/ok' and red 'not found/problem' in the third card. Orange or yellow outlines and highlights look like edited or highlighted items. The scattered multicoloured dots in the background have no clear meaning to me and look decorative.

threeSecond.purpose: Athena is a guided tool that helps you turn a rough idea into a research question backed by real papers from PubMed and OpenAlex, through a 9-step process.
threeSecond.first: Tap the blue "Start a review" button, since it is the most prominent action and the page says it is free to try.
threeSecond.next: Type in my rough research idea and go through the steps. If I was unsure, I would scroll down to "How it works: 9 steps, 3 stages" to see what the process looks like before committing.

In the preview card at the bottom, the small blue/orange/red outlined boxes look like labels or states, perhaps accepted or rejected items, but I cannot tell.

threeSecond.purpose: A sign-up page for Athena, a tool that guides you from a rough idea to a research question backed by real papers in 9 steps.
threeSecond.first: Click into the Email field, which already looks focused, and type my email address. I might skip the optional name.
threeSecond.next: Type a password of at least 10 characters that avoids the name part of my email, then click the blue "Create account" button.
confusing: What a '9 steps' process involves is not clear from this page.
'Your reviews are private to your account' - I did not know what 'reviews' meant (literature reviews?).
The Email field has a bright white outline, which looks odd until I realise it is the focus state.
The labels and password hint are small and low-contrast grey, so I would have to squint.
There is no show-password toggle, no sign-up alternative such as Google, and no sign of terms or a privacy policy.
The 'A' logo mark is tiny and says nothing about what the product does beyond its name.
threeSecond.colors: The blue-purple button is the main call to action. The white outline on the Email field means it is active or selected. Everything else is dark background with grey and white text, with no other meaningful colours.

threeSecond.purpose: A login page for Athena, a literature-review tool, where a returning user signs in to continue their saved review.

threeSecond.next: Click the blue "Log in" button again with corrected details. If I still could not get in, I would read the small grey text about forgetting a password, or click "Create an account" if I had never signed up.

threeSecond.purpose: A dashboard called Athena listing "My projects", where each project is a 9-step literature review (idea to research question) that you open to continue where you left off.
threeSecond.first: Click the blue "Start a new review" button, or, to continue existing work, open the card that says "Your turn: step 9, research question" (or the one with the orange warning).
threeSecond.next: Open a project card and carry on with the step it says is my turn. If I had made a new review, I would fill in my topic. I might also look at the orange-warning card to fix the changed step, or use "Sort and filter" to tame the list.
confusing: Nine of the ten cards have identical titles ('What is the knowledge gap in implementing telemedicine in Southeast Asia?'), so I can't tell them apart except by progress bar and step.
The row of small bars: I can guess it is 9 steps of progress, but I don't know what the grey segment (vs. the dark ones) means.
Step names like 'scoping', 'appraisal', 'synthesis', 'summary table', 'ranking', 'search builder' are jargon I don't understand.
The '...' menu on each card: I don't know what it offers until I open it.
'Sort and filter' is collapsed and '10 of 10' is slightly unclear at a glance.
'Step 2 changed, so 7 later steps need updating' is a worrying message and I'm not sure what to do about it.
Several cards show 'Your turn' with a clock-like icon, and I'm not sure what the icon means.
The last card is cut off at the bottom of the screen.
threeSecond.colors: Green bar segments = completed steps. A grey/light segment = the current step (where it's my turn). Dark/empty segments = steps not yet done. Orange/amber on one card (bars and text with a warning triangle) = a warning or problem: something changed and needs attention. The blue button = the main call to action. Everything else is a dark neutral theme with no meaning.

problems.problem: The 'How it works' illustrations contain text at roughly 6-8px (step names, 'Paper A', 'Sleep duration', the quoted sentences, 'Accept / Edit / Delete'). It is unreadable at every width and is an image of text. These pictures are the only preview of the product on the page, so a first-time visitor cannot learn from them.
problems.fix: Redraw each illustration with a few large labels (at least 14px at rendered size) and cut the fine detail. Alternatively use real HTML text and shapes so it scales and can be zoomed. Give each image a meaningful alt text.

problems.problem: The stage cards are inconsistent. A card titled 'Stage 1 of 3 · Shape your question' shows a picture labelled 'STEP 2 OF 9: Turn it into search topics'. Stage 2 shows step 6 and stage 3 shows step 7. The small 'Pictured: step N' caption under each image is the only thing that explains this, and it is easy to miss. The three stages and the nine steps read as two competing systems.
problems.fix: Make the caption part of the card's heading line, for example 'Stage 1 of 3 · Shape your question (example: step 2)'. Or show a 9-step strip on each card with the pictured step highlighted.

problems.problem: Jargon the landing page never defines: 'Appraise the selected papers', 'visible rubric', 'what is known, contested and unknown', 'synthesis'. The brief asks for jargon to be explained inline, and the hero explains PubMed and OpenAlex but these later terms get no explanation. The nine step names are only listed as 12px grey run-on text ('1. Describe your idea · 2. Turn it into search topics...'), which is hard to scan.
problems.fix: Replace 'Appraise' with plain wording such as 'Check each paper', or add a short gloss: 'appraise = check how reliable a paper is'. Replace 'rubric' with 'scoring checklist'. Show the 9 steps as a numbered list or strip with readable contrast.

problems.problem: The hero is a four-line headline followed by a seven-line paragraph before the first button. 'Free to try...' is 12px grey text under the buttons. The two buttons are the same width and height, so only fill colour separates the primary from the secondary. The paragraph is dense for a first screen.
problems.fix: Cut the paragraph to two short sentences and move the PubMed/OpenAlex gloss and 'You confirm each of the 9 steps' into the 'How it works' section. Make 'I have an account' a text link or a lighter ghost button so 'Start a review' is clearly the one dominant action.

problems.problem: The decorative coloured dot field sits directly behind the hero paragraph, and some dots cross words ('drafts', 'research'). The 'Pictured: step N' caption in each card is cramped against the divider below it (about 2px at 768).
problems.fix: Fade or mask the dot field behind the text block, or lower its opacity. Add 6-8px of padding below the caption.

problems.problem: Field spacing is too tight. Each label sits about 4px above its own field and only about 8px below the previous field. Labels for 'Email' and 'Password' therefore look attached to the field above. Labels and the helper text are about 12px mid-grey on near-black, which is marginal for AA at that size.
problems.fix: Use about 16-20px between field groups and about 6px between label and field. Raise label and helper colour and size (13-14px, at least 4.5:1).

problems.problem: The password hint 'At least 10 characters, not containing the name part of your email' is awkward for novices. There is no show/hide password control and no live indication of whether the rule is met. 'Create account' gives no hint about what happens next (the user lands on a new review, per ?next=/s/new).
problems.fix: Rewrite as 'At least 10 characters. Don't use the first part of your email address.' Add a 'Show password' toggle. Add a short line under the button such as 'Next: describe your research idea.'

problems.problem: The wrong-password error is clear (icon, text and border). But the email and password fields do not change state: no red border, no aria-invalid cue, and the password dots stay in the field. 'Forgot your password? Ask the person who runs this Athena server to reset it' is 12px grey text and leaves a novice with no action to take. The heading wraps and leaves 'review' alone on a second line at 768 and 1366.
problems.fix: Mark both fields as invalid with a visible red outline and tie the message to them with aria-describedby. Clear or focus the password field. Make the forgot-password text normal body size, with a concrete next step such as an admin contact link. Shorten the heading to 'Log in' or 'Welcome back' to avoid the orphan word.

problems.problem: The same cramped label-to-field spacing as on signup: the 'Password' label looks like it belongs to the email field above. There is no show-password toggle after a failed attempt, which makes it hard for a user to see what they typed.
problems.fix: Apply the same spacing fix as signup. Add a 'Show password' toggle.

problems.problem: Cards in the same row stretch to equal height, but the progress bar and status line are bottom-aligned. Cards with a two-line title therefore show an unexplained empty gap between the date and the bar. The 'Step 2 changed...' stale card is also taller than its neighbours, which makes the grid ragged.
problems.fix: Top-align the bar directly under the date, or reserve a fixed-height title block with a line clamp. Place the stale warning in a fixed footer row.

problems.problem: The segmented progress bar uses colour alone to separate done (green), current (light grey), future (dark grey) and stale (amber). There is no legend and no 'N of 9' text. The future segments are nearly invisible against the card (well under 3:1). In the stale state all 7 later segments turn amber, so the bar no longer shows how far along the project is. The only second cue is the small status line.
problems.fix: Add 'Step 5 of 9' to the status text. Give the current segment a distinct shape or outline. Raise the contrast of future segments to at least 3:1. For stale, keep the done segments green and mark only the changed step and the later ones with a hatch pattern plus the warning text. Add a one-line key under the page intro or in the Sort and filter panel.

problems.problem: Many cards carry the same bold title, and the only differences are small grey metadata and step text. That makes it hard to pick the right project. The card has no visible 'Continue' action; the '...' button is the only visible control, and it is about 20px wide. This is a real risk when users run the same idea several times. The unlabeled avatar icon in the header also gives no hint it opens the account menu.
problems.fix: Add a visible 'Continue' or 'Open' text button (or a chevron) on each card. Make the '...' target at least 44x44px at 375px. Show the step name or last-edit time more prominently when titles repeat. Give the avatar button an aria-label and a visible tooltip or text such as 'Account'.

problems.problem: The header is inconsistent with the other signed-in pages. Here the logo is followed by the text 'My projects', which reads like the product name or the page title. On Account and Settings the same text has a back arrow, and the logo moves to the centre at 768 and 1366. Users cannot tell whether 'My projects' is a link, a title or the brand.
problems.fix: Use one header pattern: a back arrow plus 'My projects' on the left (as on Account/Settings), and the same logo placement at every width. On the new page, 'Athena' should stay the brand.

problems.problem: The step strip is only the text 'Step 1 of 9 · Your idea' in small grey type. There is no 9-segment progress strip like the one on the project cards. Done and next are not shown as a strip (only a faint 'Next:' hint at the bottom). 'Start my review' looks fully enabled while the line under it says 'Write at least a sentence to start.' The hint sits close to the button and is easy to miss, so a user may press it with an empty box. The example chips are about 28px tall, below 44px.
problems.fix: Show a compact 9-step strip with step 1 highlighted and the next step name ('Next: Turn it into search topics') directly under the heading. Show the button in a clearly disabled style (or keep it enabled and show an inline error on empty submit). Add aria-disabled and move the hint inside the form region. Increase chip height to about 40-44px at 375px.

problems.problem: 'Save name' and 'Change password' are drawn as dim grey ghost buttons with grey text on dark. It is not possible to tell whether they are disabled or just low emphasis. Their text and border contrast looks under 4.5:1 and 3:1. There are no show/hide password controls. The AI usage table lists many projects with the same title, and the 'AI calls' and 'Cost' columns are narrow with the header wrapped onto two lines.
problems.fix: Use a clear secondary button style with at least 4.5:1 text contrast when enabled, and a visibly different disabled style plus helper text. Add a show-password toggle. In the usage table, include a differentiator (current step or date/time) and keep column headers on one line.

problems.problem: At 375 the header has only the back arrow, 'My projects' and avatar. At 768 and 1366 a logo appears in the centre of the bar. The Athena wordmark is not shown on Account or Settings at any width, but it is on Login and Signup.
problems.fix: Use one header composition across widths and pages, or drop the centre logo.

problems.problem: The 'How this server runs Athena' panel shows 'Demo mode' (scripted AI) next to a green tick and 'AI is on - AI steps run when you start them'. These two statements read as contradictory, because the AI is scripted and not real. The panel has no heading-level emphasis for the mode a novice should care about. 'Each search fetches up to 40 papers' is 12px grey footnote text.
problems.fix: Combine them into one status line, for example 'Demo mode: AI answers are scripted samples, so results will not match your topic.' Show 'AI is on' only when real AI is active. Move the 40-paper limit into a normal-size line, defined as a limit per search.

problems.problem: Each topic row puts the topic name, the orange 'suggested' badge, Edit, Keep and Delete on one line. The name is squeezed into about 90px and wraps to 3-4 lines ('Barriers / and / facilitators / to / implementation'), so five topics fill the first screen and only 3-4 are visible. The Edit and Delete text links are about 25-40px wide, well under a 44px touch target, and Delete sits right beside Keep with no undo.
problems.fix: On narrow widths stack each row. Put the full-width topic name on line 1, with the 'suggested' badge above or beside it. Put Edit, Keep and Delete on line 2 as 44px-tall buttons with spacing between them. Style Delete as a quiet destructive action and add an Undo toast. Keep the badge text, since it is the second cue.

problems.problem: Five identical outlined 'Keep' buttons, one per row, look like primary actions. They compete with the filled 'Keep 5 suggested topics' footer button, which does the same thing for all rows. The brief calls for one visually dominant action per page.
problems.fix: Make the per-row Keep a quiet text or ghost button. Alternatively, show a per-row check only after a topic is kept. Leave the filled footer button as the single dominant action.

problems.problem: The canvas topic cards say 'Accept' and 'Dismiss', while the side panel says 'Keep' and 'Delete' for the same action. The side panel also covers the right part of the canvas cards, so the badge reads 'Sugg…' and the button reads 'Dis…'. Users see two sets of controls with different words and cannot read either set in full on the canvas.
problems.fix: Use one vocabulary everywhere (for example 'Keep' / 'Remove'). Pan or fit the canvas so the cards sit fully left of the panel when the panel opens, or hide the card actions while the panel is open.

problems.problem: The page shows one query ('Query: Telemedicine adoption and use') but the only primary action is 'Run all 10 searches'. Nothing says which of the 10 you are viewing, that nine more exist, or how to move between them. At 375 the list is not visible at all. At 1366 the 'Run all 10 searches' button sits inside a single query card, which implies it runs only that query.
problems.fix: Add a 'Search 1 of 10' label with Previous / Next controls or a compact list of all queries with their counts. Remove the run button from the single card. Keep 'Run all 10 searches' only in the sticky footer.

problems.problem: A three-line Demo mode box and a collapsed 'What happens in this step' row sit above the first real content. At 375 the PubMed count and its warning start at about y=500, and the OpenAlex count and the query terms are entirely below the fold. The user cannot see what they are being asked to check without scrolling.
problems.fix: On mobile, collapse the demo box into a one-line chip or a dismissible strip. Show a compact count summary first (PubMed N, OpenAlex N, with the broad warning). Put the term groups behind a 'Show search terms' disclosure.

problems.problem: The orange warning says 'Broad: only the 40 most relevant will be collected... Add a term to focus it', but no control for adding a term is visible. The demo note also mentions 'your edits to the search text, years or languages', but no edit, year or language controls appear. The page tells users to act and offers no way to do it. The term chips do not look editable or non-editable.
problems.fix: Add a visible 'Add a term' or 'Edit search' button next to the warning, and show the year and language filters. If editing is not available in the demo, remove the 'add a term' and 'your edits' wording, or say plainly 'editing is turned off in demo'. Add a clear editable look (+ and x on chips) if they can be changed.

problems.problem: Jargon is only partly defined. 'index term' is explained, but 'MeSH' appears undefined in the list rows ('5 synonyms · 1 MeSH'). 'Query', 'OpenAlex', 'PubMed' and 'dry-run counts' are not explained. The heading says 'searches' while the subtitle and list say 'Query', and the footer says 'queries'.
problems.fix: Use 'search' everywhere. Define MeSH inline ('MeSH = PubMed's official topic labels'). Add one line saying PubMed and OpenAlex are the two paper databases being searched.

problems.problem: The broad-match warning is a three-line paragraph in orange body text, with no icon. The word 'Broad:' is the only non-colour cue. 'Count again' is an outlined button sitting inside the sentence flow and reads like part of the warning.
problems.fix: Add a warning icon and a short bold label ('Too broad'). Keep the explanation in neutral text. Move 'Count again' below the message, or rename it 'Recount papers'.

problems.problem: The step strip in the panel header shows steps 1-3 green and step 4 white, while the label says 'Done'. A completed step is drawn as in-progress. The page top bar at 768 and 1366 says 'Now: step 5/9' while the panel says 'Viewing step 4 of 9'. Together these make it unclear which step is current and which are done.
problems.fix: Colour completed steps green, including the one being viewed. Mark 'viewing' with an outline or underline rather than a different fill. Add a step name under the bar ('Done: Scoping, Search, Retrieval. Next: Summary table'), and keep step 4 as the current page.

problems.problem: Step 5 has four names: 'summary table' (strip), 'Summary & ranking' (canvas and list), 'rank the papers' (footer and canvas button), and 'summarise each abstract' (subtitle). The headline says 'then summarise the papers', but the primary button 'Go to step 5: Summary table' only navigates and does not start summarising. 'Next:' appears twice (under the subtitle and in the footer) with different wording.
problems.fix: Pick one name ('Summary table') and use it everywhere. Headline: 'Check what was found'. Button: 'Next: build the summary table'. Drop the duplicate 'Next:' line, or make both lines identical.

problems.problem: The subtitle promises 'how many papers each database returned', but no per-database breakdown (PubMed vs OpenAlex) is visible. There is no sign of whether any of the 10 searches failed or returned zero papers. The text and the two stat tiles repeat the same 195 and 205 numbers. The empty/error/partial states the brief requires are not shown.
problems.fix: Add a small table of searches by database (PubMed N, OpenAlex N) near the top, with a visible 'All 10 searches finished' or '1 search failed - retry' status line. Drop the duplicate tiles or the sentence.

problems.problem: The text says 'Click or tap an article type to show only those papers', but the Article type rows are plain grey labels and bars with no button look, hover state or selected state. The explanatory note is about 11px grey text below the chart. Article-type rows are also indented differently from the study-type rows, which have a marker.
problems.fix: Make the rows real toggle buttons with a border or hover style and a visible selected state. Add 'Show all' / 'Clear filter'. Place the instruction above the chart. Align both charts to the same grid.

problems.problem: The study-type legend uses colour plus small shapes (about 8px), which is good, but 'Other design' (green plus) and 'Cross-sectional' (green triangle) use similar greens, and the bar fills are the only place the colour appears. The shapes are tiny and are not repeated on the bars.
problems.fix: Use clearly different hues for neighbouring categories, or hatch patterns. Make the markers at least 12px and show the same marker at the bar start. Keep the text labels.

problems.problem: The canvas and list use undefined or abbreviated terms: 'Corpus', 'dupes removed', 'Ran: PubMed 979 ...'. Plain wording elsewhere ('the same paper found twice') is better. The 'Finished 9:45:02 AM' stamp has no date, and the '8 s' on 'What happens in this step' is never explained.
problems.fix: Replace 'Corpus' with 'Papers found', and 'dupes' with 'duplicates'. Add a date or relative time ('Finished 2 min ago'). Explain '8 s' ('8 sec read') or remove it.

problems.problem: The ⋯ and × buttons are in the header's top-right and shrink the title and description column to about 240px, so the headline takes 3 lines and the progress bar is only about 240px wide while the content below is 340px wide. There is also no global header, back button or step navigation at this width, and the meaning of × (close what?) is unclear.
problems.fix: Put ⋯ and × on their own row, or fold them into one overflow menu, so the title uses the full width. Add a labelled 'Back' or 'Project' control. Give × an accessible name and a visible label such as 'Close panel'.

problems.problem: The sticky footer takes about 110px of the 812px screen (two lines of helper text plus buttons). 'What we know so far' is cut off mid-line behind it, so the first answered fact looks unfinished. With the on-screen keyboard open there will be very little room left for the chat.
problems.fix: On mobile, remove the footer helper line or move it into the 'What happens in this step' disclosure. Add bottom padding so the last content is not clipped. Check the layout with the keyboard open.

problems.problem: Counts disagree between screens: 'question 1 of up to 5' versus '3 questions' on the scoping conversation row and '6 of 6 answered' on 'What we know so far'. The textarea says '(Enter sends)', which is surprising on a phone, where Enter normally adds a new line. 'What happens in this step' has an unexplained '8 s'.
problems.fix: Use one consistent count and wording ('Question 3 of up to 5'). Say 'Press Send answer' on touch devices, and use Shift+Enter hints only on desktop. Explain or drop '8 s'.

problems.problem: The top step strip shows only numbers 1-9 with check marks. Step names, what is done, and what is next appear only for the current step, and only in small grey text in the panel. A novice cannot tell what steps 3-9 are.
problems.fix: Show the current step name and the next step name in the strip ('Step 3 Search builder → next: Retrieval'). Add a tooltip or label with each step's name on hover and focus. At 768, where the strip is only a thin bar, add the same text line.

problems.problem: In List view the left list (about 288px wide) is cut off by the side panel. Rows end mid-word without an ellipsis ('Telemedicine adoption and us', 'Query PubMed 979 · OpenAlex 1', 'Ran: PubMed 979 · OpenA', 'Corpus 195 papers, 205 dupes rem'). Important counts, such as the OpenAlex number, are lost.
problems.fix: Truncate with a visible ellipsis and a full-text tooltip, or let titles wrap to two lines. Give the list a minimum width, or collapse it to icons when the panel is open. Put the counts on their own line.

problems.problem: The canvas zoom toolbar (+ / - / fit / map) sits on top of cards at the bottom left ('Policy, regulation...' in Search, and the 'Digital infrastructure' card in Retrieval). Cards on the left are clipped at the viewport edge ('opic', 'ers and facilitators') with no hint that the canvas scrolls.
problems.fix: Offset the toolbar from the card area, or give it a solid background and reserve space. On open, fit the canvas so the current step's cards are fully visible.

problems.problem: Key guidance is set in about 11-12px grey on near-black: 'Next: ...', 'What we know so far', 'question 1 of up to 5', field hints, chart notes, footer helper text. Contrast may be near the 4.5:1 AA limit and the size is hard to read on a phone. The unfilled segments of the step bar are very dark grey on black, below 3:1 non-text contrast.
problems.fix: Raise helper text to at least 13-14px with a lighter grey (verify 4.5:1 or better). Lighten the inactive step segments to 3:1 or more, and keep a text label for the step.
